newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Hoechst/Clariant Australian merger near completion.
newsitem.headline: Hoechst/Clariant Australian merger near completion.

text.p: Chemical groups Hoechst AG and Clariant AG said on Thursday the majority of the approvals for the merger of their specialty chemical businesses in Australia had been obtained.
Last December, the German-based Hoechst agreed to sell its specialty chemical business to Clariant, a Swiss company, in return for a minority stake in Clariant.
"The merger will see Clariant become one of the world's largest specialty chemicals manufacturers with an annual turnover in excess of A$9 billion," the companies said in a joint statement.

The expanded Clariant started its Australian operations on July 1 and is now a major supplier in industries ranging from plastic, inks, textiles, leather, construction, telecommunications and detergents.
Clariant now operates four plants in the state of Victoria and one in New South Wales.
